parts.part: Rail on desktop, drawer on tablet, bottom navigation on phone

leaves.what: Edited the block (src/components/AppShell.tsx): the rail now starts at 840px instead of 600px, and between 600 and 840 the destinations are in a modal NavigationDrawer opened by a menu IconButton (AppShellMenuButton, exported from the block) placed in the top bar's leading slot. Added isDrawerOpen / onDrawerClose props and a brand(withName) prop replacing railHeader.
leaves.why: The block's comment: "Yours to change: a drawer in place of the expanded rail, a FAB in the rail's `header`, an account button in its `footer`, other widths." The block as shipped has no drawer form and nothing that opens one.

leaves.what: A browser ResizeObserver (not a React Aria hook) in the block closes the modal drawer when the shell's width leaves 600-840px.
leaves.why: The modal drawer is a portalled overlay: the container queries that show and hide the rail and the bar cannot hide it, and the kit has nothing that ties a drawer to a width.

leaves.what: A brand mark (an 'L' on primary, with the name beside it on the expanded rail and in the drawer) written by hand for the rail's and drawer's header slots.
leaves.why: Expected: the kit has no logo part.

leaves.what: Read NavigationDrawer's and NavigationRail's source past the doc comment.
leaves.why: To learn that a modal drawer calls onClose itself when a destination is chosen, that a destination with href is a React Aria Link (so the router adapter routes it), and what the header slots lay out.

parts.notes: Not seen in a browser (none allowed): the three forms are switched by container queries on the shell's width (<600 bar, 600-839 menu button + modal drawer, >=840 rail, >=1200 expanded rail). 'Drawer on tablet' was read as a modal drawer; a standard 360dp drawer would leave a 600-840px window too little content. The expanded rail at >=1200 is the block's own and was kept.

leaves.what: Wrapped each leading IconButton (menu, back) in a span carrying container-query classes (hidden @[600px]:flex @[840px]:hidden; flex @[600px]:hidden) so the bar shows the menu button only on a tablet and the back button only on a phone on a nested page.
leaves.why: TopAppBar's doc: "The `leading` and `actions` slots take the interactive parts — pass `IconButton`s". Which one shows at which width is the project's logic around it; the bar itself has no responsive leading.

leaves.what: The bar's title is the current route's name (its h1), taken from route handles; document.title is set beside it.

parts.notes: Small variant only; no on-scroll behaviour (the kit documents it as not built).

leaves.what: The nav 'Path' landmark around the kit's Breadcrumbs, under the top bar and outside main, built from the matched routes (Clients > client > invoice). Shown only where the path has two levels or more.
leaves.why: The Breadcrumbs doc asks for it: "put it in a `nav` with a name, so the path is a landmark". A one-level path would only repeat the title.

parts.notes: Top-level pages therefore show no breadcrumbs; open /clients/hartwell-sons or an invoice under it to see two and three levels. On a phone the bar also shows a back button to the level above.

leaves.what: The menu's trigger is react-aria-components' Button, round, 48dp, holding the kit's Avatar (32dp) with the kit's StateLayer and focusRing.
leaves.why: The kit has no pressable avatar: IconButton takes only an icon component ({size, className}) and draws it at 24dp in the icon colour, Avatar is not pressable, and Button is a labelled pill.

leaves.what: Menu's header prop holds the account line (avatar, name, email); className="min-w-56" widens the surface; placement="bottom end".
leaves.why: Menu's doc: "`header` static content above the items, `placement` and `offset` where the popover sits, `className` extra classes on its surface".

leaves.what: Sign out really leaves the shell: a signed-out page (EmptyState with a 'Sign in again' Button) replaces it. The theme item toggles the .dark class on <html>.
leaves.why: Project logic; a mock session held in state.

parts.notes: Items: Profile and settings (a routed link to /settings), Use dark/light theme, divider, Sign out. The theme choice is not persisted across a reload (only ?dark is).

leaves.what: VisuallyHidden from react-aria-components for a polite status that says the page's name after a client-side navigation, and for the brand's name on the collapsed rail.
leaves.why: The skill lists it under 'What comes straight from React Aria': "Text only a screen reader gets | VisuallyHidden | For a status, or a name with no visible text." (so arguably not a leave).

parts.notes: Landmarks: banner (TopAppBar's header), navigation 'Main' (one of rail/bar rendered visible at a time, the others display:none; the drawer's nav exists only while open), navigation 'Path' (breadcrumbs), main (focusable, the skip link's target). The skip link is the block's: first in the tab order, shown on focus. Focus is not moved to main on navigation; the page's name is announced and main is scrolled to the top. Not checked with a screen reader.

leaves.what: react-router's createBrowserRouter with a layout route that mounts AriaRouterProvider around the shell; each route carries a handle (title, destination) that the bar, the breadcrumbs and the selected destination read through useMatches.
leaves.why: Project logic; the adapter's doc says: "Mount once, inside the router and above the components".

leaves.what: href passed to GridListItem so a client or invoice row is a routed link.
leaves.why: GridListItem's doc: "React Aria's `GridListItem`, which gives the row its focus, its selection, its action and its drag"; it hands React Aria's props down. The doc does not name href, so this leans towards option: I relied on knowing React Aria's GridListItem takes href.

leaves.what: Sample pages by hand: Overview (three figures, invoices to chase), Clients (list), a client's page and an invoice's page, each with Skeleton placeholders on a 700ms timer; Invoices, Reports and Settings are honest EmptyState placeholders.

parts.notes: Every link is a real <a> routed client-side through the adapter: destinations, breadcrumb levels, the menu's profile item, the phone's back button, list rows, EmptyState actions. The mailto link on a client's page goes through the same RouterProvider; React Aria is expected to leave an external scheme to the browser, not verified here. A deep link needs the host to serve index.html for any path (vite dev/preview do).

general_leaves.what: Page column, figure cards (Card as li), definition lists and invoice lines laid out by hand with role utilities and the type primitives.

None that failed: the first build was green. One self-caught mistake before the log: dt/dd placed inside Card inside a dl (invalid nesting, Card adds two divs), rewritten as a ul of Card component="li".
general_leaves.why: Card's root can be an li but its content part is always a div, so it cannot sit directly in a dl.

friction: Nothing was verified in a browser, so every visual and keyboard claim is from reading code. The shell block offers rail and bar but 'a drawer in place of the expanded rail' is left to the reader: a modal drawer needs open state, a trigger that lives in someone else's top bar, and closing when the width changes, none of which the block sketches; a ready 'menu button' export and an isDrawerOpen pair would have made part 1 a prop. The kit has no avatar button (an account trigger is in nearly every shell): IconButton accepting children or an avatar would remove the one react-aria Button. GridListItem's doc does not say rows can take href, though that is how a list of links is built. Breadcrumbs do not collapse on a phone and the doc gives no advice for narrow widths. The react-router adapter's header comment speaks of an augmentation living in adapters/next.tsx, a file this project does not have.
